McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammel, Green, Fletcher and Holland, were the most prominent. The race proceeded with the first position undecided and not until two miles from home could Green, Pope and Hyde shake off the others.
A feature of this race was the excellent team work of Hyde, and this gave Enfield their only win of the evening. In the 4 x 440yds. we had to call upon F R.

Len Fletcher and Tommy Green were chasing Hyde from the commencement of the race, but were not able to catch him. These two, with the help of Paul Khlopin (17th) and Frank Elson (20th) gave us the scratch team awards, whilst C.
Len Fletcher was in good form and finished second to Hyde, after a tremendous struggle with Pope, of Woodford Green A.C. We finished six men in the first sixteen—excellent team work.
However, Len Fletcher again followed Hyde home, and led our team to their third scratch team win. Frank Thorn showed a return to form in finishing fifth and was our second man home.

The same course as last year was used and Hyde, Fletcher and Pope took the lead in turn. They were still together with Fletcher, if anything, a yard in front, when Hyde suffered disqualification for the second year in succession.

The programme also included a 2 miles Team Walk to which we received an invitation, together with Woodford Green A.C., Enfield A.C., Highgate H., Surrey A.C. and the promoting club, Polytechnic H., Hyde, of Enfield, won, followed by Cooper and Pope, of Woodford Green, and Fletcher, of our Club.
Hyde, the winner, is a newcomer, while F. Stroud continued his successes by being second with another newcomer in A.
Something went wrong at the bend in the first heat and Garland and Hyde fell, which, of course, knocked both of them out of the final.

The race itself was notable for the stern tussle which took place between Hyde and Tommy Green, Tommy eventually winning by 10 seconds. Len Fletcher finished third, and Harry Churcher, walking as an individual, did well to be sixth.

In this Walk Hyde succeeded in reversing the "Highgate" result, and finished in front of Green. Fletcher had an uneasy time in the early stages of the race, but recovered later and did well to finish fifth.

They were Hyde (Enfield A.C., scratch), and our own Fletcher (20 secs.) and Green (30 secs.). We take pleasure in congratulating Hyde and Co. upon their recent wins. During past years they have been placed second to us on many occasions; and it is only meet that they should have their share of success—the reward of perseverance.
Green walked a splendid race in beating Hyde, while Harry Churcher (4th), Jack Field (5th) and Frank Elson (7th), also gave our colours prominence.

In the race at Bellingham, Fletcher beat Hyde in convincing fashion, and our scratch team finished 1, 5, 6 and 7—most satisfactory. Redgrave was second in the individual handicap and was a member of our team placed second in the team handicap.

David Cocks running the race of his life, gave everything he possessed and took us up to 2nd only 3 secs. behind the Luton boy Hyde, who had previously caught and passed him to put up a first-class performance.
McMullen, Hyde, Pope, Scammell, Green, Fletcher and Holland were the most prominent. Our 'A' team packed in fine fashion to win the scratch team race (3,6,7,9).
